These findings suggest that 4-Hydroxy-L-threonine may act as a modulator or indirect activator of Lysosomal alpha-glucosidase through a chain of target interactions. The evidence supports a mechanism where 4-Hydroxy-L-threonine influences the activity of a G protein-activated channel, which in turn affects the function of Lysosomal alpha-glucosidase. While the exact nature of this interaction remains unclear, the shared target of multiple compounds points to a possible regulatory pathway involving ion channels and enzyme activity.
